*BCBA owned and operated!*

Who we are

LaughLoveLive Again is a behavioral and mental health therapy provider that proffers therapy with an ABA twist. We believe that learning histories do not define your future. We believe that skills can be learned to improve learning repertoires that lead to socially significant behavior change.

*

*
What we do

We provide a combination of behavioral and mental health approaches for a variety of issues from anxiety, to developmental disorders like Autism Spectrum Disorder and other developmental disabilities and co-occurring disorders. We specialize in providing interventions for domestic violence and individuals that struggle with high instances of maladaptive and aggressive behaviors with autism spectrum disorder

*

*
How we do it

By utilizing up-to-date, empirically based practice, we create individualized treatment plans to ensure your training and therapeutic approach is right for you. Whether individualized or in a group setting, each client is special and deserves that attention. Services are provided in-home, in-office, in-community, in-school and online via Telehealth by board certified and licensed professionals who CARE

Job Description

Please read thoroughly before applying!

We are seeking an upbeat and compassionate Behavior Therapist to provide behavior-analytic services to a verbal adult on the autism spectrum in Miami, FL. The primary focus of this case is supporting the client in developing and strengthening executive functioning, adaptive functioning, independence, and other identified treatment goals. The ideal therapist will be comfortable providing regular 1:1 services to an adult client and collaborating with family members, a BCBA, and other professionals involved in the client’s care. The therapist will also be expected to work collaboratively with the BCBA to incorporate a behavior-analytic and mental health-informed approach into sessions to support the client’s overall success.

Schedule & Hours

This is an in-home case with morning hours and up to 25 approved hours per week. With potential for additional hours in the evening. The expected schedule is approximately 7:00/8:00 AM–12:00 PM. The therapist must be willing to work some Saturdays when necessary, including participation in Saturday morning trainings. Monthly case roundtable meetings will take place at 6:30 PM. Please only apply if you are available for the required schedule and able to commit to the needs of this case.

The adult client will participate in the interview process and will have the opportunity to ask questions of potential therapists.

Requirements

Compassion-focused and trauma-informed care is an important part of the services we provide. The ideal candidate must be able to provide services with compassion, patience, respect, and understanding and be willing to learn and apply trauma-informed approaches when working with the client. At least one year of experience working with adults, individuals on the Autism spectrum, or underserved populations is preferred. Candidates with a strong desire to work with these populations and a willingness to learn and complete additional training will also be considered.

Experience working with adults and individuals on the Autism spectrum is highly preferred. Bilingual communication skills in English and Spanish are preferred. Experience working with individuals who display hoarding behaviors is preferred; however, candidates who are willing to learn appropriate, trauma-informed strategies to support the client will also be considered. The therapist must be willing to learn about pervasive demand for autonomy and how it may impact the client’s engagement, independence, and response to therapeutic demands.

The therapist must be comfortable collaborating with the BCBA, family members, and other professionals involved in the client’s care and must be open to learning and applying behavioral principles. A foundational understanding of behavior-analytic principles is preferred, including familiarity with the main functions of behavior, the ABCs of behavior (Antecedent, Behavior, and Consequence), and effective strategies for building rapport and establishing a positive therapeutic relationship with a client. Additional training may be required prior to or throughout employment to ensure you have the knowledge and tools needed to provide high-quality services.

The ideal candidate will have an upbeat attitude, strong communication skills, and the ability to build rapport with clients and their families. An ABA background or a strong interest in pursuing growth within the field is preferred. An RBT credential and at least a bachelor's degree are highly desired.

Responsibilities

The Behavior Therapist will provide 1:1 behavior-analytic services in the client’s home and/or community under the supervision and guidance of a BCBA. Responsibilities include collecting data accurately and in real time, implementing the behavior intervention plan and treatment plan with fidelity, and communicating with the BCBA regarding observations, progress, barriers, or other relevant changes related to treatment.

The therapist will collaborate with the BCBA, family members, and other professionals involved in the client’s care and may assist with developing and reviewing service plans, treatment plans, behavior intervention plans, and skill-based assessments as needed throughout treatment. The therapist may also assist with documentation and reports for schools, courts, or other community agencies when necessary. Attendance at required group meetings, trainings, and monthly case roundtables is expected.

Pay

Pay is based on experience, willingness to learn, and demonstrated fluency in the skills learned through training.

LaughLoveLive Again is a strong advocate for continuous learning and professional growth. We offer performance-based pay rather than pay based solely on tenure, providing employees with opportunities to increase their earning potential as they develop their skills and demonstrate consistent application of what they have learned.

Benefits

Paid RBT Competency Assessment: Receive coaching and training before completing your competency assessment. The experience and training gained while working with us can help you feel more confident when you are ready to take your exam. A pay increase is available upon obtaining your RBT credential.

Performance-Based Pay: Compensation is based on what you learn and how consistently and confidently you apply your skills, rather than solely on how long you have been with the company. Employees are evaluated every six months for opportunities for advancement and increased compensation. As you grow as a therapist, we hope you will grow with the company.

Career Advancement: Supervision is provided for individuals pursuing the BCaBA or BCBA credential. You will gain hands-on experience and have opportunities to learn and develop the skills needed to advance within the field.

Collaboration: You will have opportunities to participate in group meetings and trainings where team members can share ideas, discuss challenges, collaborate on client needs, and learn from one another.

Experience

At least 1 year of experience working with adults, individuals on the Autism spectrum, or underserved populations is preferred. Candidates with a strong desire to work with these populations and a willingness to learn and complete additional training will also be considered.

The ideal candidate will have an upbeat attitude, strong communication skills, and the ability to build rapport with clients and families. An ABA background or a strong interest in pursuing professional growth within the field is preferred. An RBT credential and at least a bachelor's degree are highly desired.

Education & Credentials

A high school diploma is required. A bachelor's degree, or active enrollment in a bachelor's degree program, in psychology, early childhood development, applied behavior analysis, or a related field is highly desired. An RBT or BCaBA certification through the BACB and in good standing is preferred.

Work Setting

This is an in-person, in-home position. Remote work is not available.

This is a great opportunity for someone interested in working with an adult on the Autism spectrum while gaining experience with a collaborative, multidisciplinary approach focused on executive functioning, adaptive functioning, independence, and overall quality of life. If you’re interested in learning more about this opportunity, we’d love to hear from you!

• Competitive Compensation: $25 - $27 per hour, based on your experience, education, and certifications, paid biweekly by direct deposit.

As a Lead RBT, you are the go-to person in the field. You run your own ABA sessions with families, and you are also the RBT other RBTs call when a program or a behavior gets tricky. • Experience: Experience mentoring or training other RBTs.

• Passion for Children: A genuine love for working with kids and families.

• Ethics and Integrity: Upholding client rights, confidentiality, and the BACB Ethics Code.

• Becoming a Trusted Professional: Showing reliability, consistency, and follow-through to build trust with families and your team.
• Learning on the Fly and Adaptability: Quickly learning new client protocols and adjusting when session dynamics change.
